title: The Cursed Caravan
description: A merchant caravan has been cursed while crossing the Pale Causeway. Supplies rot, animals die, and strange omens appear. The players must escort the caravan to safety while uncovering a conspiracy involving a powerful entity that feeds on suffering. Folk horror and survival with multiple moral resolutions.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: The Hungering Dark
bestiary.description: An ancient entity that feeds on suffering, despair, and life force. It spreads its curse through manipulation, emotion, and possession.

sb_spends.name: Whisper of Despair
sb_spends.effect: Target gains 1 Fatigue and must test Resolve or mark Dread.

sb_spends.name: Grip of the Curse
sb_spends.effect: All enemies in Near zone suffer -1 die to actions for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: Manifest Hunger
sb_spends.effect: The entity manifests partially, dealing Harm 2 to all in zone and advancing the Curse Escalation timer by 1.

bestiary.name: Mistwraith
bestiary.description: Secrets made flesh; they feed on awareness and fear. They appear where the party hesitates or falters.

sb_spends.name: Ethereal Touch
sb_spends.effect: Target loses 1 Fatigue and gains a Condition: Haunted.

bestiary.name: Shadewalker
bestiary.description: Corpse-puppets bound in root and bone. Slow, relentless, territorial.

sb_spends.name: Relentless Advance
sb_spends.effect: Ignore one point of Fatigue and gain +1 die to next attack.

acts.title: The Cursed Caravan
acts.description: Players encounter the caravan and experience the curse's immediate effects. They must decide to help and begin investigating the source.

scenes.title: The Desperate Merchant
scenes.description: The party finds the caravan stalled on the road. Merchant Aldric Thorne offers a reward for help. The curse manifests as supplies rot and animals die.

outcomes.clean: You stabilize the immediate crisis and gain the merchant's trust.
outcomes.partial: You save some supplies, but the curse shows its teeth.
outcomes.miss: Animals die and supplies rot further. Tick Curse Escalation +1 and Caravan Supplies -1.

scenes.title: The Hedge-Witch's Warning
scenes.description: Hedge-Witch Mira Blackwood approaches in a tavern, warning of the dark force moving along the trade routes.

outcomes.clean: You learn that the curse is tied to a sealed chest and can be contained with folk rituals.
outcomes.partial: You gain some information, but she demands a favor.
outcomes.miss: She clams up, sensing you are not ready for the truth.

acts.title: Into the Blackwood
acts.description: The party seeks help from the hedge-witch and faces the growing influence of the Hungering Dark.

scenes.title: The Chest Investigation
scenes.description: The party examines the mysterious sealed cargo item that is the source of the curse.

outcomes.clean: You discover the chest contains a bound entity and learn how to perform a containment ritual.
outcomes.partial: You learn the nature of the curse but trigger a minor backlash. Tick Curse Escalation +1.
outcomes.miss: The chest lashes out, causing Harm 1 to the party and advancing Hungering Dark's Strength +2.

scenes.title: The Protective Ritual
scenes.description: Using the hedge-witch's knowledge, the party performs a protective ritual to resist the curse.

outcomes.clean: You gain Folk Protection Tokens (salt, red thread, butter-left charm) and reduce the Curse Escalation by 1.
outcomes.partial: The ritual works but consumes materials and leaves you exposed.
outcomes.miss: The ritual fails, and the entity takes notice. Tick Hungering Dark's Strength +1.

acts.title: The Cursed Crossroads
acts.description: The final confrontation at the Cursed Crossroads, where the party must choose between containment, bargain, or destruction.

scenes.title: The Confrontation
scenes.description: The party faces the Hungering Dark's strongest influence at the crossroads.

outcomes.clean: You successfully contain the curse through ritual or destroy the entity. Resolution achieved.
outcomes.partial: You strike a bargain with the entity, buying safety at a cost.
outcomes.miss: The entity escapes, and the curse spreads further. The caravan is lost.

outcomes.clean: You negotiate a terrible bargain that ends the immediate threat but leaves a lasting debt.
outcomes.partial: You narrowly escape, but the entity's influence remains.
outcomes.miss: You are overwhelmed; the curse claims you.

npcs.name: Merchant Aldric Thorne
npcs.motivation: Save his livelihood and family reputation
npcs.secret: He knows the chest was given to him by a stranger who warned him not to open it.

npcs.name: Hedge-Witch Mira Blackwood
npcs.motivation: Protect the community from supernatural threats
npcs.secret: She knows more than she reveals; she has personal stake in the curse.

npcs.name: Margravine Xara Rothari
npcs.secret: She is aware of the curse but sees it as a tool to control the region.

locations.name: The Pale Causeway
locations.description: The last high road that survives the spring thaws. Crossings are perilous, and the road seems to shift and change.

locations.name: Blackwood Hollow
locations.description: A charcoal burner's clearing with a hedge-witch's dwelling, protected by strong wards.

locations.name: The Cursed Crossroads
locations.description: Meeting point of multiple roads, a place of choice and consequence where the Hungering Dark's influence is strongest.

factions.name: The Merchant's Caravan
factions.relationship: The characters are hired to protect them.

factions.name: The Hungering Dark
factions.goals: Feed on suffering and break free of its prison.
factions.relationship: The party must confront or contain it.

campaignTimers.name: Curse Escalation
campaignTimers.description: Advances when the party fails to contain the curse or when the entity feeds.

campaignTimers.name: Caravan Supplies
campaignTimers.description: Depletes as supplies rot. When empty, the caravan cannot continue.

campaignTimers.name: Hungering Dark's Strength
campaignTimers.description: Increases when the entity gains power through fear and suffering.

notes: A folk horror survival module with multiple resolutions: contain the curse, strike a bargain, or destroy the entity. The tone is bleak and desperate.

pacing.act1: The curse manifests through rot, decay, and omens—show, don't explain. Aldric is desperate but evasive; his secret (the stranger who gave him the chest) is a clue, not a confession. Mira Blackwood is a source of folk wisdom, not a solution—she offers protection, not answers. The Chest Investigation is Act II's centerpiece; do not reveal its contents or the entity's nature in Act I. Emphasize the ticking clocks: Caravan Supplies dwindles visibly, Curse Escalation advances with every failed mitigation. The Pale Causeway should feel like a living, watching place—the road itself is a character.
pacing.act2: This is the revelation phase. The Chest Investigation reveals the bound entity. Mira's protective rituals offer a temporary buffer but consume resources. The Hungering Dark's Strength timer advances when the party's fear gives it power—describe the entity's influence as emotional and atmospheric, not just mechanical. Mistwraiths appear when the party hesitates or falters—they are secrets made flesh, not random monsters. The party should feel the weight of the curse pressing in; the ritual is their only defense, not their solution.
pacing.act3: The Crossroads is a place of choice. The three resolutions (containment, bargain, destruction) each have distinct tones: containment is bleak but safe; bargain is desperate and costly; destruction is heroic but risky. The Hungering Dark's final manifestation should feel earned—if the party has researched and prepared, they have leverage; if they rushed, they face the full brunt. The Cursed Child encounter is a mirror to the party's own moral compromises—use it to test their resolve, not as a simple combat.

npcSecrets.aldric-thorne: His secret is a hook, not a reveal. He will not volunteer the stranger's identity unless pressed or given reason to trust. If the party saves the caravan, he may confess in Act III as a moment of redemption.
npcSecrets.mira-blackwood: Her personal stake is a late Act II or Act III revelation. She is a guide in Act I, a ritualist in Act II, and a potential sacrifice or ally in Act III depending on the party's choices. Do not reveal her secret until she has reason to share it.
npcSecrets.margravine-xara: She is a background threat. Her secret (using the curse as a tool) is a late Act III revelation if the party investigates regional politics. She is not a primary antagonist unless the party makes her one.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: The chest contains a bound entity (the Hungering Dark) — its contents are an Act II discovery
The exact nature of the containment ritual — Mira offers folk protection, but the full ritual requires investigation
The Hungering Dark's true nature (ancient entity feeding on suffering) — describe its effects, not its origin
The Bargain resolution option — present it as a moral discovery, not a listed choice upfront
Margravine Xara's manipulation of the curse

title: Silk & Velvet
description: Urban intrigue across the trade-bridge city of Silkstrand, a night of high etiquette at Ravenswood Manor, and the stair-ruled metropolis of Thepyrgos. The players must navigate contracts, masks, and glamour to prevent a ritual that would swap the souls of the city's elite.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: Glamour Ghost
bestiary.description: An illusion given form, used by the Crimson Masque troupe to confuse and misdirect.

sb_spends.name: Illusory Double
sb_spends.effect: Create a duplicate that forces opponents to reroll attacks.

acts.title: A Song of Poison and Plague
acts.description: Urban investigation as the Gemcutters and Alchemists edge toward riots, while a bard of Desire plays both sides.

scenes.title: The Redwater Audit
scenes.description: The party must enter the dyeworks with forged or earned permits to investigate the source of the poisoned water.

outcomes.clean: You gain entry and find evidence linking the alchemists to the poison.
outcomes.partial: You enter but alert a guard; tick City Unrest +1.

scenes.title: The Alleyway Serenade
scenes.description: Sel Virelle 'rescues' a bystander to win the party's trust. Reading her tells can downshift DV.

outcomes.clean: You see through her performance and gain leverage over her.
outcomes.partial: You earn her trust but she escapes your scrutiny.
outcomes.miss: She charms you and gains a hold on the party.

acts.title: The Gilded Cage
acts.description: A night of velvet hospitality at Ravenswood Manor. Each room is a social encounter with taboos and tells.

scenes.title: Conservatory of Masks
scenes.description: Choose alliances and navigate the etiquette of masks. Violating taboos advances Etiquette Breach.

outcomes.clean: You gain an important alliance and learn a rival's schedule.
outcomes.partial: You avoid insult but miss a key clue.
outcomes.miss: You commit a faux pas; tick Etiquette Breach +1.

acts.title: The Crimson Masque
acts.description: A public ritual threatens to swap souls. The party must infiltrate rehearsals and stop the rite on stage.

scenes.title: The On-Stage Challenge
scenes.description: Dismantle the ritual pillars (Bell Cadence, Mask Index, Applause Escrow) before the final bell.

outcomes.clean: You stop the ritual and expose the Masque Director.
outcomes.partial: You stop it but at great cost; some souls are swapped.
outcomes.miss: The ritual completes; the city's elite are replaced.

npcs.name: Guildmistress Kavra
npcs.secret: She knows about the poison but sees it as a way to discredit the Alchemists.

npcs.name: Master Orun
npcs.secret: He is producing the poison but blames the Gemcutters.

npcs.name: Sel Virelle
npcs.secret: She is orchestrating the chaos for the Crimson Masque.

locations.name: Silkstrand
locations.description: A city of canals, dyed waterways, and legal bridges. Permits and seals are visible power.

locations.name: Ravenswood Manor
locations.description: A noble estate where the party must survive a night of velvet hospitality and intricate social traps.

locations.name: Thepyrgos
locations.description: A stair-ruled metropolis where bell-law and stair-rights can crown or crush reputations overnight.

factions.name: The Crimson Masque
factions.goals: Swap souls of the elite for power.

campaignTimers.name: Sel's Glamour Net
campaignTimers.description: Advances when Sel gains influence over the party or city.

campaignTimers.name: Midnight Duel
campaignTimers.description: Advances as the rival's plot reaches its peak.

campaignTimers.name: Etiquette Breach
campaignTimers.description: Advances when the party violates social taboos at Ravenswood.

campaignTimers.name: Act Countdown
campaignTimers.description: Advances as the performance night approaches.

notes: Urban intrigue module with strong social mechanics. Can be run as three separate arcs or a single campaign. Emphasis on Position, DV, and leverage via Diamonds.

pacing.act1: This is the investigation phase. The poison is a symptom, not the cause—guild tensions are the real battlefield. Sel Virelle is a charming antagonist; she should seem helpful until the party reads her tells or investigates her. The Crimson Masque is a shadow—their name may be whispered, but their true goal (soul-swapping) is an Act III discovery. Emphasize the City Unrest timer: the streets are a powder keg. The Gemcutters and Alchemists are both guilty and both victims—avoid a simple 'good vs evil' framing.
pacing.act2: Ravenswood Manor is a social pressure cooker. The Etiquette Breach timer is the primary threat—violating taboos invites consequences, but breaking them strategically may open doors. The Conservatory of Masks is a chance to build alliances and gather intelligence. The Midnight Duel timer represents the rival's plot coming to a head—it's not a literal duel unless the party makes it one. Sel's Glamour Net may still be active; if she charmed the party in Act I, this is where she cashes in that hold. The Crimson Masque's ritual mechanics (Bell Cadence, Mask Index, Applause Escrow) should remain abstract until Act III.
pacing.act3: This is the climax. The Act Countdown timer creates urgency—the ritual is underway, and the party must dismantle its pillars. Breaking the pillars requires understanding the ritual's structure (gained through investigation in Acts I-II). The three pillars are mechanical challenges: Bell Cadence (disrupt timing), Mask Index (expose the performers), Applause Escrow (turn the audience). The ending should reflect the party's choices: a clean success exposes the Masque Director; a partial success swaps some souls (a haunting consequence); a miss means the city's elite are replaced by the Masque's agents.

npcSecrets.guildmistress-kavra: Her secret (using the poison to discredit the Alchemists) is a mid-Act I discovery if the party investigates her. It makes her a potential ally—or a target—depending on the party's morals. She is not a villain; she is a pragmatist.
npcSecrets.master-orun: His secret (producing the poison but blaming the Gemcutters) is a parallel to Kavra's. The truth is that both guilds are being manipulated by the Crimson Masque. This revelation should land in Act II or early Act III.
npcSecrets.sel-virelle: Her secret (orchestrating chaos for the Crimson Masque) is the Act II/III linchpin. If the party reads her tells in Act I, they may suspect her; if they fail, her charm offensive continues. She should be a mirror to the party—talented, ambitious, and willing to burn the city for a stage.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: The Crimson Masque's soul-swapping ritual — Act III only
That Sel Virelle is working for the Crimson Masque — Act II/III reveal
The specific mechanics of the ritual pillars (Bell Cadence, Mask Index, Applause Escrow) — Act III only
The poison's true source is the Crimson Masque manipulating both guilds — Act II/III discovery
Ravenswood Manor's hidden passages or secrets — should be discovered through exploration, not exposited

title: The Dwarven Debt
description: A dwarven merchant house calls in an ancient debt, demanding the party retrieve the Forgefather's Voice, a sacred artifact from the dangerous Spine Underway. The party must navigate dwarven law, honor, and the supernatural forces that guard the artifact.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: The Stone-Singer
bestiary.description: An ancient entity bound to the stone, communicating through resonance and dreams. It guards the Forgefather's Crypt.

sb_spends.name: Stone Resonance
sb_spends.effect: All enemies in zone take Harm 1 and must test Athletics or be pinned.

sb_spends.name: Dream of the Deep
sb_spends.effect: Target falls into a vision, losing their next action.

acts.title: The Debt Called
acts.description: The party is summoned by Clan-Speaker Thrain Ironhold to fulfill an ancient contract. They must navigate dwarven customs and the financial desperation of House Khaz-Vurim.

scenes.title: The Legal Consultation
scenes.description: Clan-Speaker Thrain explains the contract's details and the history of the Forgefather's Voice.

outcomes.clean: You fully understand the contract and its loopholes.
outcomes.partial: You grasp the basics but miss a key clause.
outcomes.miss: You insult the dwarves; tick Dwarven Honor -1.

acts.title: Into the Deep
acts.description: The party descends into the Spine Underway, facing ancient mechanisms and supernatural disturbances.

scenes.title: The Spine Underway
scenes.description: Navigate the dangerous tunnels and encounter the first signs of the Deep Stirrings.

outcomes.clean: You bypass the mechanism safely and gain a clue to the artifact's location.
outcomes.partial: You trigger a trap but survive; tick Ancient Ward Stability +1.
outcomes.miss: The mechanism collapses a passage; tick Stone-Song Resonance +1.

acts.title: The Forgefather's Crypt
acts.description: The party reaches the sacred resting place of the Forgefather's Voice and must decide its fate.

scenes.title: The Crypt Confrontation
scenes.description: The party faces the Stone-Singer and must choose between restoration, legal victory, or supernatural compromise.

outcomes.clean: You perform the ancient ritual to restore the artifact, satisfying all parties.
outcomes.partial: You secure the artifact but at a cost; tick Debt Resolution +1.
outcomes.miss: You anger the Stone-Singer; combat begins and the artifact is lost.

npcs.name: Vault-Queen Thora Stonebeard
npcs.motivation: Honor house obligations while preserving tradition
npcs.secret: She knows the artifact was never properly transferred.

npcs.name: Clan-Speaker Thrain Ironhold
npcs.secret: He is prepared to enforce the house rights if necessary.

npcs.name: Forge-Master Durin Emberheart
npcs.secret: He knows the true nature of the Forgefather's Voice and its connection to the Deep Stirrings.

locations.name: Khaz-Vurim Halls
locations.description: Ancestral home carved from massive stone formation. Perfect stonework and intricate metalwork.

locations.name: The Spine Underway
locations.description: Vast network of ancient tunnels connecting dwarven holds. Remnants of pre-dwarven civilizations.

locations.name: The Forgefather's Crypt
locations.description: Sacred resting place of the Forgefather's Voice, protected by ancient wards and the Stone-Singer.

factions.name: House Khaz-Vurim
factions.goals: Restore financial stability and honor ancient contracts.
factions.relationship: The party is bound by debt to them.

factions.name: The Deep Stirrings
factions.goals: Protect the artifact and the balance of the deep places.
factions.relationship: They may be allies or obstacles.

campaignTimers.name: Debt Resolution
campaignTimers.description: Advances as the legal pressure mounts.

campaignTimers.name: Ancient Ward Stability
campaignTimers.description: Advances when the party disrupts the crypt's defenses.

campaignTimers.name: Stone-Song Resonance
campaignTimers.description: Advances as the artifact calls to return home.

campaignTimers.name: Dwarven Honor
campaignTimers.description: Tracks the party's standing with dwarven society.

notes: A moral and legal drama set in dwarven culture. Themes of honor, tradition, and supernatural balance. Multiple resolution paths: restoration, legal victory, or supernatural compromise.

pacing.act1: This is a legal and cultural introduction. The Debt Resolution timer represents the legal pressure—House Khaz-Vurim's financial desperation is palpable, but they will not break tradition. Thrain is a diplomat; he will not reveal the contract's loopholes unless pressed. Thora's secret (the artifact was never properly transferred) is a major Act III reveal—hint at it through her evasiveness, not her confession. Dwarven Honor is a social currency; insults or breaches of etiquette can close doors. The Forgefather's Voice is described as a 'sacred artifact'—its true nature (a binding instrument of the Deep Stirrings) is an Act II/III discovery.
pacing.act2: The Spine Underway is ancient, dangerous, and alive. Ancient Ward Stability represents the crypt's defenses—the party can bypass them with care or brute force. Stone-Song Resonance is the artifact's call—it grows stronger as they approach, affecting their dreams and decisions. The Deep Stirrings are not a single faction but a presence—the Stone-Singer is their voice. The ancient mechanisms are puzzles, not combat encounters; reward creativity and dwarven lore.
pacing.act3: The Forgefather's Crypt is the climax. The Stone-Singer is not a monster to be slain—it is a guardian to be reasoned with or appeased. The three resolutions: Restoration (perform the ancient ritual, satisfying all parties), Legal Victory (use the contract's loophole to claim the artifact without supernatural cost), Supernatural Compromise (bargain with the Stone-Singer). Each has different costs and consequences. The Debt Resolution timer ticks as the legal pressure mounts; if it fills before the party acts, House Khaz-Vurim may take drastic measures.

npcSecrets.thora-stonebeard: Her secret (the artifact was never properly transferred) is the legal loophole. She will not reveal it unless the party earns her trust or discovers it through research. It is the key to the Legal Victory resolution.
npcSecrets.thrain-ironhold: His secret (prepared to enforce house rights) means he is not an ally—he is a neutral arbiter. He will enforce the contract as written, not as the party wishes. He is a source of information, not a source of sympathy.
npcSecrets.durin-emberheart: His secret (the true nature of the artifact and its connection to the Deep Stirrings) is the key to the Restoration resolution. He knows the ancient rituals and the artifact's purpose. He is a reluctant ally—he wants balance, not power.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: The Forgefather's Voice is a binding instrument of the Deep Stirrings, not merely a sacred artifact — Act II/III discovery
The artifact was never properly transferred (Thora's secret) — Act III legal reveal
The Stone-Singer is a guardian, not a monster — its nature is discovered through interaction, not combat
The specific ritual required for Restoration — Act III discovery through Durin or ancient texts
The contract's loophole (the legal resolution) — Act I/II investigation find

title: Ashes of the Infernal Accord
description: An epic-tier adventure where the party is drawn into infernal politics. Maelstraeus offers a deal to stop Mor'iraath's expansion, but accepting grants Obligation. The party must navigate the City of Cinder, confront the Demon of Fire and Destruction, and decide whether to uphold or break their infernal bargains.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: Mor'iraath's Avatar
bestiary.description: An avatar of the Demon of Fire and Destruction, a being of entropic consumption.

sb_spends.name: Conflagration
sb_spends.effect: Deal Harm 2 to all enemies in a zone and advance the Consumption Timer.

sb_spends.name: Infernal Audit
sb_spends.effect: Target loses 1 Obligation and suffers a curse.

acts.title: Descent
acts.description: The party journeys to the City of Cinder, facing early encounters with Mor'iraath's agents and the whispers of Livaea.

scenes.title: The Journey
scenes.description: Travel through the shifting landscapes to the City of Cinder, encountering a minor Mor'iraath agent or a Livaea whisper test.

outcomes.clean: You resist Livaea's temptation and learn a useful secret.
outcomes.partial: You are tempted but resist; tick Livaea's Manipulation +1.
outcomes.miss: You accept a deal; gain 1 Obligation to Livaea.

acts.title: The Infernal Bazaar
acts.description: Navigate the City of Cinder's factions, gather information, and make deals. Livaea's influence foreshadows the final manipulation.

scenes.title: The Grand Exchange
scenes.description: The party must broker a deal with a faction to gain access to the Fractured Court.

outcomes.clean: You secure a powerful ally and gain a Market Stabilizer.
outcomes.partial: You gain some leverage but tick Cinder Market Stability +1.
outcomes.miss: You anger a faction; tick Cinder Market Stability +2.

acts.title: The Fractured Court
acts.description: The final confrontation: choose between Direct Confrontation or Infernal Subterfuge. Livaea's manipulation is revealed, and the party must decide whether to complete Maelstraeus's goal or defy him.

scenes.title: The Revelation
scenes.description: Livaea's scheme is exposed; the party must make a hard choice.

outcomes.clean: You successfully navigate the court and contain the threat.
outcomes.partial: You contain the threat but incur major Obligation.
outcomes.miss: The infernal accord shatters; Mor'iraath's expansion continues.

npcs.name: Maelstraeus
npcs.motivation: Build webs of interdependence and stop Mor'iraath.
npcs.secret: He has his own hidden agenda beyond stopping Mor'iraath.

npcs.name: Mor'iraath
npcs.motivation: Consume all value and reduce the world to ash.
npcs.secret: He is the principle of entropic consumption, not just a being.

npcs.name: Livaea
npcs.motivation: Tempt and manipulate all parties for her own ends.
npcs.secret: She is the unseen hand behind many deals.

locations.name: City of Cinder
locations.description: A sprawling marketplace built from the calcified remnants of broken dreams. Currency is concepts: fragments of soul, moments of joy, oaths.

locations.name: The Fractured Court
locations.description: The seat of power where the fate of the infernal accord is decided.

factions.name: Maelstraeus's Web
factions.relationship: The party may owe Obligation to him.

factions.name: Livaea's Manipulators
factions.relationship: She may be an ally or enemy.

campaignTimers.name: Mor'iraath's Expansion
campaignTimers.description: Advances as Mor'iraath's forces gain ground.

campaignTimers.name: Cinder Market Stability
campaignTimers.description: Advances as the City of Cinder becomes unstable.

notes: Epic-tier infernal politics module with cosmic stakes. Focus on Obligation and hard choices. The City of Cinder generator provides faction and location variety.

pacing.act1: The journey to the City of Cinder is a descent into a world where concepts are currency. Mor'iraath's Expansion is the background threat—his agents are scouts, not armies. Livaea's whispers are temptations; failing the Whisper Test grants Obligation, which will matter in Act III. Maelstraeus is a distant patron—his offer is not a trick, but it has strings. The City of Cinder's nature (calcified remnants of broken dreams) should feel surreal and ominous, not cartoonishly evil. Cinder Market Stability is a fragile peace; the party's actions in Act II affect it.
pacing.act2: The Infernal Bazaar is a place of trade, not combat. Factions have needs and prices—the party must navigate them. The Grand Exchange is the key encounter; success gives leverage, failure destabilizes. Livaea's influence should be felt, not seen—she is the whisper behind the deal, the temptation in the fine print. Foreshadow the final revelation: Livaea's manipulation is not a betrayal—it's the natural conclusion of her nature. The Market Stabilizer is a resource; if the party secures it, they have an edge in Act III.
pacing.act3: The Fractured Court is the crucible. The party must choose between Direct Confrontation (fight Mor'iraath's Avatar) or Infernal Subterfuge (use Maelstraeus's network to outmaneuver him). Livaea's manipulation is revealed—she played both sides, and the party's Obligation to her (if any) is leverage. The three outcomes: clean (contain the threat, minimal cost), partial (contain the threat but incur major Obligation), miss (the accord shatters, Mor'iraath's expansion continues). The choice should feel earned based on the party's actions in Acts I-II.

npcSecrets.maelstraeus: His hidden agenda is not evil—it's self-preservation. He wants to stop Mor'iraath, but he also wants to emerge stronger. His secret is a late Act III revelation if the party investigates him. He is not a villain; he is a pragmatist.
npcSecrets.moriraath: His secret (he is the principle of entropic consumption) means he cannot be destroyed, only contained or redirected. This is the key to the Infernal Subterfuge resolution. Reveal this through lore, not combat.
npcSecrets.livaea: Her secret (the unseen hand behind many deals) is the Act III twist. She has been manipulating all factions. The party's Obligation to her is her leverage. She is not a boss fight—she is a moral test.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: Maelstraeus's hidden agenda — Act III revelation if investigated
Mor'iraath is a principle, not a being — Act II/III lore discovery
Livaea is manipulating all parties — the Act III twist
The Infernal Subterfuge resolution path — present it as an option discovered through investigation, not a menu choice upfront
The specific cost of Obligation to Livaea in Act III — foreshadow, but do not spell out

title: The Ninth Bell
description: In Theona, a cultural taboo has been broken. The Ninth Law states: 'The ninth word is never spoken, the ninth path is hidden, and the ninth name is erased from history.' A bell has begun ringing where no bell should ring, marking the countdown to the Green Host's arrival. The horror is inevitable; the only choice is how to appease the land.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: The Green Host
bestiary.description: Not a physical entity but a force of cultural consequence. The land's enforcement mechanism for broken oaths.

sb_spends.name: Claim the Unmourned
sb_spends.effect: Target is marked for death; must make Resolve DV 5 or be claimed.

acts.title: The Bell Rings
acts.description: The party encounters the ringing bell and the silent village. They learn of the Ninth Law and the countdown to the ninth chime.

scenes.title: The Silent Village
scenes.description: Arriving at a village where no one speaks, the party discovers the bell tolling at the edge of town.

outcomes.clean: You find handprints in the snow leading to the bell but ending where no human could stand.
outcomes.partial: You learn the bell is a warning; tick Bell's Countdown +1.
outcomes.miss: You trigger a supernatural echo; tick Bell's Countdown +2.

acts.title: The Land Remembers
acts.description: The land's memory becomes active; cold spots, visual distortions, and the Green Host draws near. The party must find the person who broke the Ninth Law.

scenes.title: The Unmarked Grave
scenes.description: The party finds a fresh grave with no marker, dug by the land itself.

outcomes.clean: You learn the name of the dead person and the ninth name that was spoken.
outcomes.partial: You find a clue but not the full name.
outcomes.miss: The land hinders you; tick Bell's Countdown +1.

acts.title: The Ninth Chime
acts.description: Dawn approaches. The party must perform the proper ritual of appeasement to prevent the Green Host from claiming the village.

scenes.title: The Ritual of Appeasement
scenes.description: The party must speak all nine names, perform the Silent Vigil, and take the Ninth Path.

outcomes.clean: The land is appeased; the bell stops ringing. The village is saved.
outcomes.partial: The Green Host claims only the one who broke the law; the bell stops.
outcomes.miss: The Green Host claims the entire village; the bell rings eternally.

locations.name: The Silent Bell
locations.description: A bell hanging from a single iron post on a windswept hill. No rope, no striker—yet it rings.

locations.name: The Village of Stone-Silent
locations.description: A village where no doors are locked but no voices are heard. Ritual silence is observed.

locations.name: The Unmarked Grave
locations.description: A fresh grave in a field with no marker, dug by the land itself. A ninth flower grows in the center.

factions.name: The Law-Keepers of Theona
factions.relationship: They may help or hinder the party.

campaignTimers.name: Bell's Countdown
campaignTimers.description: Advances each hour until dawn. When full, the Green Host arrives.

notes: A short, low-fantasy horror module about cultural consequences. Combat is minimal; the focus is on investigation, ritual, and moral choice.

pacing.act1: The village is silent—this is the first mystery. The party must discover the Ninth Law and the bell's significance. Jordan is the Keeper; he is evasive, not hostile. The Bell's Countdown is the primary tension—it ticks relentlessly, and the party must manage their time. The Green Host is a concept, not a creature; its arrival is inevitable if the taboo is not addressed. The handprints in the snow are an omen—the land is already responding. Do not reveal Jordan's secret or Elyra's punishment yet.
pacing.act2: The land's memory becomes active. Cold spots, visual distortions, and the Unmarked Grave are manifestations of the broken taboo. The party must investigate the grave to learn the ninth name and the identity of the one who spoke it. Elyra is a source of cultural wisdom, but her silence is a punishment—she will not speak directly. The Green Host draws nearer; describe its approach as atmospheric (distant thunder, wilting crops, a chill in the air) rather than a physical threat. The Bell's Countdown accelerates; each investigation consumes precious time.
pacing.act3: Dawn approaches. The Ritual of Appeasement requires the party to speak all nine names, perform the Silent Vigil, and take the Ninth Path. This is a ritual challenge—combat is minimal or absent. The three outcomes: clean (the land is appeased), partial (the Green Host claims only the guilty), miss (the village is lost). The tone is bleak and final; there is no 'winning' in a traditional sense—only making the least terrible choice.

npcSecrets.jordan: His secret (his son spoke the ninth name) is the heart of the mystery. He will not confess unless the party uncovers the truth through investigation (the grave, the bell, or village records). His guilt is palpable—use his body language, not his confession.
npcSecrets.elyra: Her secret (her silence is punishment) is a tragic parallel to Jordan's guilt. She is a source of ritual knowledge but cannot speak it directly. The party must interpret her gestures, her silence, and the village's traditions to understand the Ritual of Appeasement.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: Jordan's son spoke the ninth name — Act II/III discovery
The exact steps of the Ritual of Appeasement — Act III discovery through investigation and Elyra's guidance

The ninth name that was spoken — the climax of the investigation
